decisions.decision: Scope change: WP-5 splits into WP-5.a (compiler v1 — six stages, all node kinds, seven recipes, error catalogue, decompiler lifts) and WP-5.b (decompiler over the six declared corpus forms, round-trip >= 0.90, the five WP-5 gates); both stay in scope
decisions.why: WP-5's compiler-all-kinds surface plus the corpus round-trip exceeds one context window and CONTROL section 6 forbids half-committing, so the split is data declared before the work, mirroring D-070
decisions.consequence: ten ids in scope; no work leaves the session

decisions.decision: Test change: the golden-defect predicates are kind-aware. N1 exempts labelled INPUT types (registry `editModeChannel:"input"`) not just SFS node `field`; N8 infers the kind from the emitted loader/submitter signature and checks the matching profile rather than hardcoding the list's `dataSubmitterType:"none"`; A1's `items` non-vacuity moves from per-fixture to SET-level (like `slots`, D-080)
decisions.why: the predicates were written when only the list golden existed and baked in list expectations; create/detail/datalist forms satisfy the SAME rules with different profile values, and an input legitimately shows its label
decisions.consequence: the N1..N11 rules and A1..A5 identities hold for every kind; non-vacuity of slots AND items is asserted across the fixture set

decisions.decision: The error catalogue (§2.7) is GENERATED from `packages/sfs/src` by `tools/gen-catalogue.mjs` — one row per `new <X>Error(code, message)` — and a test asserts byte-identity to a fresh generation plus coverage of every raised code
decisions.why: a prose list of error codes rots the first time a code is added; deriving it from the raise sites makes drift a failing test (INV-2)
decisions.consequence: 34 codes catalogued; a new code with no row fails `catalogue.test.mjs`

decisions.decision: Node-kind resolution for the input-ish leaves: `field` resolves its type from `component` (offline; `_datatypeMap` needs a backend, MET-2203); `select` resolves to `dropdown` (referenceList) or `autocomplete` (entity) by `source`; the decompiler lifts `dropdown`/`autocomplete` back to `select` so the emit path — and thus the type-specific key order — is identical on round-trip
decisions.why: the SFS node enum stays fixed while any registry input type is reachable via `field`; lifting dropdown to field+raw would reorder type-specific keys and break Q1 byte-equality
decisions.consequence: all six new node kinds round-trip byte-equal (selfconsistency over the clean set)

decisions.decision: Gate removal: WP-5's five planned gates resolve as — g-corpus-immutable and g-escape-budget shipped; g-determinism's enforcement is `determinism.test.mjs` (D-021) and g-no-literal-hex's is `tokens.mjs` TOK-2010 (D-010/D-019), both already-live programs not duplicated as gates; g-markup-provenance is deferred to BL-008 (no committed `*.form.json` artifacts exist in Scope A to recompile)
decisions.why: INV-2 is satisfied when a rule has A program enforcing it, not necessarily a NEW gate; duplicating live enforcement as gates adds theatre, and a provenance gate with nothing to walk is zero-coverage
decisions.consequence: every pending:WP-5 decision now names a live enforcer; two net-new gates ship

decisions.decision: The `components-kb` relocates to `packages/sfs/kb` and the examples to `packages/sfs/corpus` (both L1) as WP-7a deletes `shesha-form-edit`; both stay read-only extractor/round-trip inputs, now self-contained under `packages/` with no toolchain code reaching into a plugin skill. `capability-matrix.json` is unaffected (D-087). Supersedes D-089
decisions.why: D-089 kept the KB under plugins/** to avoid inverting ownership into L0 registry/data, but deleting the skill that hosted it forces a home, and packages/sfs (the compiler+registry toolchain) is its true owner — L1 does not invert ownership
decisions.consequence: gen-registry.mjs reads the KB at its new path; the registry regenerates byte-identical; disposition carries WP-7a move rows for both

decisions.decision: Scope change: WP-3a splits into WP-3a.1 (the verifier registry read-API `load()` + `slots.json`/`required-props.json`/`deny.json` and the single tree walker `walk.mjs`) and WP-3a.2 (T1 schema tier, T2 registry 22 checks, `verify.mjs`, the coverage gates); both stay in scope. `WP-3a` is kept in wp-table as an inScope:false umbrella so the eight pending:WP-3a T2/verify decisions still resolve until WP-3a.2 ships their enforcers
decisions.why: WP-3a.1 read-layer+walker is green and committable now, but T2 22 checks + verify + gates + 42 fixtures exceed one context; CONTROL §6 forbids half-committing and blesses the WP-N.a/.b split with a Scope change row (mirrors D-070, D-090)
decisions.consequence: eleven ids in session-scope; no work leaves the session; prove.mjs requires WP-3a.1 and WP-3a.2

decisions.decision: Scope change: WP-3a.2 completes the registry for the non-priority types the clean/corpus forms use (container, dataContext, card, text, ...), pulling that slice of BL-004/BL-020 into scope — gen-registry reads `kb.settingsFields[].path` names and MERGES authored props; container gains alignItems/flexWrap/direction and dataContext uniqueStateId, all verified present in the framework clone at the pinned commit. T2 dispositions: T2.17 na (subsumed by TOK-2010, output provenance is BL-023), T2.15 flags only non-empty-base stylingBox dup, T2.20 reads the recorded meta.kind and treats none/null/empty as inactive
decisions.why: T2 cannot conform against clean compiler output while the registry lacks props the compiler legitimately emits; the brief schedules WP-3a last precisely because T2 needs the completed registry, and degrading non-priority T2.04 to uninspectable would make T2 partial and fail its acceptance
decisions.consequence: verify --tiers t1,t2 on the clean form exits 0; validate 121/121, priority full 13/13

decisions.decision: Scope change: WP-3a splits a second time (after D-096) — WP-3a.2 is the tier ladder (T1 + T2 + verify.mjs), WP-3a.3 is the coverage-proof layer (g-exit-codes, g-mutation-coverage, g-defect-class-coverage, defect-classes.json, the mutation-harness kind:fixture extension, and the tier fixtures); both stay in scope
decisions.why: the tier ladder is green, tested, and passes verify --tiers t1,t2 -> exit 0 now, while the coverage gates + fixtures + harness extension are a further context; CONTROL §6 blesses the WP-N.a/.b split for a WP exceeding one context and WP-3a is the acknowledged-largest (mirrors D-070, D-090, D-096)
decisions.consequence: twelve ids in session-scope; no work leaves the session; prove.mjs requires WP-3a.2 and WP-3a.3

decisions.decision: The verifier tiers ship a coverage-proof layer: every tier `checks[]` id is covered by a verdict-flipping `mutations[].covers` entry or is explicitly `subsumed` (g-mutation-coverage, proven flipping by tier-mutations.test); the >=90% defect-class claim is falsifiable via `defect-classes.json`, each class named to the check that catches it (g-defect-class-coverage); exit codes and the verdict union {pass,fail,partial,notRun} are single-sourced, no `warn` (g-exit-codes)
decisions.why: §3.5.1 a check class with no mutation does not exist; a defect-class claim with no covering check is unfalsifiable; a fifth verdict is a fail that stays green
decisions.consequence: 31 tier mutations all flipping; three coverage gates live; roster 20

decisions.decision: Scope change: open Scope B. Scope-B WP ids live in a new packages/verify/config/session-scope-b.json read only by a new packages/verify/src/prove-b.mjs; session-scope.json stays frozen at the 12 Scope-A ids so the Scope-A proof and its frozen expected file never drift. Adds WP-0b/5c/5d/5e/2b/1c/16b to wp-table.json and a Scope-B block to CONTROL §3. Scope B is done when prove-b prints SESSION COMPLETE — SCOPE B, granted exactly one --bless of prove-b.expected.txt, additive to CONTROL §5's two spent Scope-A blesses
decisions.why: the mining run measured 7.0% round-trip over 2,071 real forms, so the backlog is real work the rebuild owes; leaving it prose is the failure invariant 2 forbids
decisions.consequence: Scope A's frozen proof and bless budget are untouched; Scope B carries its own

decisions.decision: A production `columns` grid with EQUAL flex spans decompiles to a flex `row` of equal-width `col`s (WP-5e); unequal spans stay a structural raw escape because SFS layout widths are px-fixed/fill, not 24-grid ratios, so an unequal grid is not faithfully expressible. Refines D-035 with the decompiler's lift rule and its honest boundary
decisions.why: MINING-REPORT.md §5 ranks columns the #1 IR gap (241 forms); the common case is equal halves/thirds, which a flex row expresses exactly
decisions.consequence: an unequal grid escapes rather than lifting to an invented width the round-trip gate could not catch as wrong

decisions.decision: Scope change: WP-1c delivers BL-010 (noUncheckedIndexedAccess on tree-wide; g-workspace-hygiene enforces it true). BL-001 (3-arm SAA cost, unmeasurable in-session per D-050), BL-006, BL-014 stay BACKLOG, out of Scope B
decisions.why: BL-001 cannot be measured here, so bundling blocks WP-1c forever
decisions.consequence: deferred work stays visible in BACKLOG, never dropped

decisions.decision: Scope change: WP-3b (full brief T3) splits into WP-3b.1 (compiler placement sidecar §3.3.1), WP-3b.2 (18-name predicate engine + assertions.schema.json), WP-3b.3 (the T3 tier), WP-3b.4 (lift g-check-references out of quarantine); session-scope-b.json swaps WP-3b for the four
decisions.why: placement needs an L1 sidecar first, and g-check-references cannot lift while 12 dangling refs fail its baseline; each exceeds one context (CONTROL §6, mirrors D-096/D-098)
decisions.consequence: prove-b requires all four

decisions.decision: The compiler emits the §3.3.1 sidecar (per node region, depth, parent, tabKey, cell{sizing,px,reservePx}, rowGroup, align, orientation) on every compile, validated against packages/sfs/schema/compiled-meta.schema.json; T3 and the placement predicates read placement from it, not CSS; cell.sizing is the compiler's calc(100%-Npx)/Npx/auto declaration
decisions.why: a 1fr intent reads in the DOM as a fixed px width, so placement comes from the compiler
decisions.consequence: the contract WP-3b.2/3b.3 stand on

decisions.decision: Placement predicates are the frozen 18-name registry (packages/verify/config/predicates.json), implemented in predicates/index.mjs and enumerated in assertions.schema.json; the three must agree; a contract is declarative predicate rows the verifier evaluates over the sidecar, never English/eval
decisions.why: three copies of the name set drift unless a program reconciles them (D-014)
decisions.consequence: g-no-prose-assertions bans prose assertions and fails on registry drift

decisions.decision: Scope change: WP-3b.3 (the T3 tier) splits into WP-3b.3 (offline-core tier, wired into verify.mjs, the .build/wp3b --tiers t1,t2,t3 exit-0 acceptance), WP-3b.3b (contract checks T3.20/21/22 + fixtures + g-fixture-manifest/g-verdict-integrity), WP-3b.3c (metadata substrate + the 6 backend checks, closing D-036); session-scope-b.json swaps WP-3b.3 for the three
decisions.why: offline checks are green now; backend needs a snapshot substrate; contract needs fixtures (CONTROL §6)
decisions.consequence: prove-b requires all three

decisions.decision: The T3 contract checks (T3.20 columns, T3.21 placement, T3.22 tabs) read a per-screen contract fixture (packages/sfs/test/fixtures/contracts/<screen>.contract.json: acceptance predicate rows + a declared column set) and evaluate it through the WP-3b.2 engine; verify.mjs loads it, a run-dir copy overriding the committed one
decisions.why: placement drift is caught by recomputing the contract over the freshly-compiled screen, not by trusting a reported result
decisions.consequence: g-fixture-manifest validates each contract (schema, known predicates, real screen, byte cap); g-verdict-integrity recomputes it and fails on drift

decisions.decision: The T3 backend checks (T3.01/02/06/07/09) resolve against a recorded metadata snapshot (packages/sfs/test/fixtures/metadata/<screen>.metadata.json, D-036 shape) that verify.mjs auto-loads per screen; absent a snapshot each disposes uninspectable, never a pass, and the bounded set lives in uninspectable-budget.json. T3.03/T3.05/T3.11 stay deferred — they need entity-metadata or registry data (datatype-components, action-owners) sourced not guessed (WP-2b)
decisions.why: a 1fr-style casing defect renders every cell blank (§1.2#10) yet the DOM cannot see it, so the check reads the compiler binding against recorded metadata; an unbounded "could not look" licence is how a verifier stops verifying
decisions.consequence: g-uninspectable-budget bounds the uninspectable set; the snapshot keeps BL-003 at exit 0

decisions.decision: WP-3b lifts the two BL-003 quarantined files: t3-semantic.mjs is rewritten as the T3 tier (WP-3b.3), check-references.mjs as g-check-references on the one coverage impl (WP-3b.4) — lazy-families + uncaught-SyntaxError holes closed; the overlays/versions families drop (subjects gone: blocks D-010, components-kb to packages/sfs/kb D-095); the quarantine.json BL-003 rows and superseded files are removed. Supersedes D-049
decisions.why: a holed gate emits no green signal, but the fixes needed the T2/T3 layer that now exists
decisions.consequence: 68 dead shesha-form-edit refs repointed to shesha-spec or removed; only layout-probe stays quarantined

decisions.decision: Precedent retrieval (BL-009, WP-9) is Index A: a deterministic SHAPE index over the compiled corpus, stored one-per-line in packages/precedent/data/shapes.jsonl (gitignored) — no node:sqlite, no embedding (Index B is BL-H1). RAG is never a correctness lookup: the compiler/verifier never import it, it never imports the compiler, no skill routes props/versions/enums to it
decisions.why: an exact registry answer beats a nearest-neighbour (§4.7.1)
decisions.consequence: the package ships behaviour (no E_NOT_IMPLEMENTED); an empty index is a hard error

decisions.decision: WP-6 raises the corpus round-trip 4->7 clean: the datatable-column decompile lifts an action column to a `do` (no empty bind/caption; a bind-less column's path is its index) and allows dotted refListRef names, and the action grammar gains openDialog argIgnore (version/customWidth/showCloseIcon) plus closeDialog/confirm/startEdit/cancelEdit intents and their `do`-enum entries — closing GAP-001; the four triaged forms escape only on the sectionSeparator/collapsiblePanel/tabs node-types (BL-024)
decisions.why: production dialog/edit/column action configs carried args and shapes the six-intent grammar could not express, so faithful forms escaped
decisions.consequence: g-escape-budget ratchets the escape rate 0.20->0.125 down-only

decisions.decision: Test change: the WP-9 precedent perf test's wall-clock budget is raised 50 -> 120ms because `npm test` runs test files in parallel and this single reading absorbs co-runner scheduler/GC noise (measured 50-70ms under suite load, ~40ms in isolation); D-110's design intent and the algorithm's isolated cost are unchanged, and 120ms still fails hard on the O(n^2) regression the budget guards
decisions.consequence: No wall-clock assertion that flakes under the parallel runner

decisions.decision: WP-2b lifts the registry from 12 to 93 `full` via the reproducible extractor parse-framework-props.mjs (source-parses each settings form: editor kind -> valueType, omit-never-guess); `full >= 93` and `deferredAuthorable <= 7` are §2.8.4 demands; completenessOf counts framework-verified props as full-derived and a null overlay never clobbers a source-parsed prop; paragraph is reclassified legacy, not version-unknown
decisions.consequence: No _framework-props hand-authored; no full below 93; no invented version

decisions.decision: Scope change: WP-16b is removed from session-scope-b.json (18 -> 17 ids). Its acceptance (g-brief-budget bundle enforced <= 61440 B) is infeasible by the sanctioned BL-011 extraction: the docs/rebuild-brief/*.md bundle is ~613 KB and ~330 KB is design prose that cannot move to data/*.json, so 61440 B is reachable only by moving prose out of the glob (the S7 anti-pattern invariant 2 forbids) or a 6x rewrite dropping intent other WPs cite. BL-011 stays a deferred BACKLOG row, g-brief-budget stays bundle.enforced:false, and wp-table.json already carried WP-16b inScope:false
decisions.why: forcing the target would adapt the artifact to pass the check, the S7 failure this rebuild prevents
decisions.consequence: Scope B completes over the 17 achievable ids

decisions.decision: Scope change: WP-8 (the operating layer) splits into WP-8a (run-dir + 7 handoff schemas + sfs validate/run CLI + schemas.test + g-run-dir-location), WP-8b (6 runner/decide hooks + hooks.test + g-hook-contract/g-hook-liveness + push-admissible.test), WP-8c (3 agent files via git mv + .claude/settings.json + g-agent-contract/g-specwriter-purity/g-judge-isolation/g-plugin-enabled/g-markup-provenance), WP-8d (packages/mcp 7 tools/3 transports + .mcp.json + g-mcp-cli-parity + transports.test); session-scope-b.json swaps WP-8 for the four (§4.8 rows 1-8,12-13). §4.8 proves the hooks as programs so WP-8 is offline; the live restart pass is WP-11 (§4.9, out of session)
decisions.why: far past one context (CONTROL §6, mirrors D-103/D-106)
decisions.consequence: prove-b requires all four

decisions.decision: WP-8a: the seven handoff schemas (plan/manifest/verdict/dispatch/sfs-meta/lock/blueprint in packages/sfs/schema/) are draft-2020-12, $id boxfusion.io/shesha/sfs/<name>.schema.json, additionalProperties:false at every object level, and ajv strict-compilable; the plan schema makes five defect classes structurally impossible: a screen with no contract, an all-visual contract, a prose assertion, a repair loop above 3 rounds, and two authors on one form
decisions.why: a prose/visual contract reintroduces the §1.2/§4L3 ambiguity and placement failures
decisions.consequence: schemas.test proves the seven compile under {strict:true} and the plan's five rejections

decisions.decision: WP-8a: the run directory lives at runs/<runId>/, gitignored, never the pre-rebuild .claude/shesha/runs/ (§4.10 pt7)
decisions.why: a run written to the old path is invisible to the toolchain and to .gitignore, and an un-ignored runs/ commits ephemeral run output as if it were source
decisions.consequence: g-run-dir-location fails on old-path files or an unignored runs/

decisions.decision: Scope change: WP-8b (the 6 operating-layer hooks) splits into WP-8b.1/8b.2/8b.3 (per-sub-WP goals in wp-table.json); session-scope-b.json swaps WP-8b for the three
decisions.why: past one context (CONTROL §6, mirrors D-115)
decisions.consequence: prove-b requires all three

decisions.decision: WP-8b.1: Claude Code hooks return only exit 0 (decision on stdout) or 2 (stdout unwritable); exit(1) is banned (a non-2 non-zero exit is a silent non-block); decide(payload,ctx) is pure over an injected ctx so hooks.test runs it in-process (runner/decide split); block-form-writes is the fast first line of INV 1 (D-003), enforced of last resort by g-markup-provenance (WP-8c)
decisions.why: a hook that fails silently protects nothing (§4.3.1 rule 5)
decisions.consequence: g-hook-contract bans exit(1), checks every wired hook exists and every decide has a runner

decisions.decision: WP-8b.2: `sfs validate --schema N --file P [--json]` checks JSON against packages/sfs/schema/*.schema.json (exit 0/1/2, writes nothing); enforce-screen-lock (PreToolUse) is the fan-out mutex + contract precondition (one sfs-specwriter lock/screen, a signed 3+-predicate contract before code, a 3-round cap); validate-sfs-on-write (PostToolUse) spawns it, renames rejects to *.rejected, blocks HOOK-0002 if it cannot start
decisions.why: a second author per screen or unvalidated input revives the two-author/SFS-1002 defects
decisions.consequence: g-hook-contract + hooks.test prove both decides and the exit contract

decisions.decision: WP-8b.3: push admission is one program (packages/verify/src/bin/push-admissible.mjs, imports coverage.mjs) evaluating P0–P9; pushAdmissible(verdict,{allowPartial,present}) is the single T1–T3 rule (T1 pass; T2 pass or absent-component partial; T3 pass or --allow-partial backend/metadata partial). gate-push detects a push (incl. raw curl to UpdateMarkup) and maps its exit; gate-dispatch enforces judge isolation + paths-not-contents on Task; session-start prints six lines, never blocks; `sfs run lock/release/new` manages locks
decisions.why: admission rules in a hook are untestable and drift; a blocked SessionStart makes the repo unopenable
decisions.consequence: push-admissible.test proves P0–P9, g-hook-liveness proves hooks.jsonl covers events, hooks.test the three decides

decisions.decision: Scope change: WP-8c (3 agents + 5 gates) splits into WP-8c.1 (6 agent files via git mv/rewrite + g-agent-contract/g-judge-isolation/g-plugin-enabled + enable plugin) and WP-8c.2 (g-markup-provenance closing D-003 + g-specwriter-purity + fixtures that recompile byte-identically + delete clean-form-config skill, moving its 8 assets/groups to packages/registry/data/prop-groups and repointing g-check-references); session-scope-b.json swaps WP-8c for the two
decisions.why: 6 agent files + 5 gates + generated compile fixtures past one context (CONTROL §6, mirrors D-115/D-118)
decisions.consequence: prove-b requires both

decisions.decision: WP-8c.1: the six subagents are files proved by g-agent-contract (name==basename, tools/disallowedTools present+disjoint, no MultiEdit, <=4096 B, no "## Hard stops"); sfs-specwriter/sfs-evaluator are git mv of form-author/form-auditor, sfs-planner is new, the other three rewritten. g-judge-isolation keeps the self-report token >400 chars from any evaluator/critic ref, pins dispatch.schema not.pattern, bars Bash from the evaluator; g-plugin-enabled requires enabledPlugins to enable shesha-developer
decisions.why: an agent rule addressed to a model's memory is not enforced
decisions.consequence: g-agent-contract + g-judge-isolation + g-plugin-enabled

decisions.decision: WP-8c.2: g-markup-provenance is the real INV-1 enforcer (closes D-003): it recompiles each compiled artifact's sibling SFS under its provenance meta (registrySha256/brand/compilerVersion) and hard-fails on any non-byte-identical result or missing sibling; fixtures are LF-pinned in .gitattributes. clean-form-config is deleted (shipped zero scripts, §1.7 T8); its 8 assets/groups move to packages/registry/data/prop-groups, read there by g-check-references
decisions.why: a command-line matcher cannot see a computed-path writer
decisions.consequence: g-markup-provenance recompiles every fixture; g-disposition records the move+deletes

decisions.decision: WP-8c.2: g-specwriter-purity hard-fails any logs/specwriter-*.md carrying one of the six markup fingerprints (parentId, componentName, "desktop":, stylingBox, _type":"action-config, version-near-type); run-dirty is the negative control
decisions.why: quoting compiled markup means the author read the artifact, not the IR (§4.1.1)
decisions.consequence: g-specwriter-purity over the clean log + run-dirty

decisions.decision: WP-8d: the shesha-sfs MCP surface is seven tools (compile/decompile/verify/registry_lookup/metadata_entity/precedent_search/push) with ONE implementation in packages/mcp/src/tools/*.mjs behind 3 adapters — stdio JSON-RPC (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.30.0, one external dep), loopback-only --http (any other --host exits 2), and a CLI subcommand per tool; /.mcp.json launches the stdio server; `sfs registry grammar` emits a GBNF whose header bars constraining a reasoning step
decisions.why: two surfaces with two implementations drift; a non-loopback bind exposes the tools
decisions.consequence: g-mcp-cli-parity locks the tool set == CLI subcommand set + schema-driven flags + the ESM export; transports.test proves the three transports
